title: Dengue Fever Early Warning System
text:
About This System
This early warning system combines spatiotemporal graph neural networks (ST-GAT + GRU) with monthly remote sensing data to forecast dengue fever incidence across 0 admin-1 regions in Southeast Asia.


Pipeline

Monthly zonal statistics fetched from Google Earth Engine
Climate delta correction applied (AR6 SSP2-4.5) to adjust for post-2018 climate shift
STGNN inference run on adjusted features
Results published automatically via GitHub Actions



Model

Architecture: ST-GAT + GRU (PyTorch Geometric)
Training period: 2011–2018
Features: ERA5-Land, MODIS LST, NDVI/EVI, CHIRPS, LULC, WorldPop
Spatial scope: SEA admin-1 regions



Performance (test set)

Huber loss: 0.390
MAE: 1.214 (log IR)
RMSE: 2.460 (log IR)
Test months: 14 held-out months





Interpretation note: Predictions are expressed as a relative risk index (predicted log IR normalised to the 2011–2018 baseline), not absolute case counts. This accounts for structural model uncertainty arising from the 8-year gap between training data and current conditions.

title: About
text:
This early warning system is developed by the Chuang Lab at Taipei Medical University (TMU) as part of ongoing research into spatiotemporally-aware dengue fever prediction for Southeast Asia.
The system jointly models dengue dynamics across Taiwan and SEA by integrating:

Monthly remote sensing data (ERA5-Land, MODIS, CHIRPS)
OpenDengue surveillance records (2011–2018)
CMIP6 climate projections (AR6, GWL scenarios)
Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6 through SSP5-8.5)

title: About
text:
Methods
Spatiotemporal Graph Attention Network (ST-GAT + GRU)
Admin-1 regions are represented as nodes in a spatial graph. The model uses two stacked Graph Attention layers for spatial message passing, followed by a GRU to capture temporal dynamics across a sliding window of monthly observations. Hyperparameters were selected via 40-trial Optuna sweeps using masked Huber loss (to handle missing surveillance data).
Climate bias correction
A delta bias correction is applied to current observations before inference, accounting for the distributional shift between the 2011–2018 training period and present-day conditions. The per-variable, per-month delta is computed as the difference between the current climatology and the 2011–2018 training baseline. Predictions are expressed as a relative risk index rather than absolute case counts.

title: Model Results
text:
Architecture
The model is a Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network with GRU (STGATGRU):

GAT layer 1: Spatial message passing over the admin-1 adjacency graph
MLP: Node-wise feature transformation
GAT layer 2: Second spatial aggregation pass
GRU: Temporal sequence modelling over the sliding window
Linear head: Single-step log IR prediction

Hyperparameters were tuned with 40 Optuna trials using masked Huber loss (to handle missing incidence data) on a validation set of 20% of training months.

title: Model Results
text:
Bias Correction Note
When running inference on current data (post-2018), a climate delta correction is applied before features are passed to the model. The delta is computed as the difference between the AR6 SSP2-4.5 projected monthly climatology for the current year and the 2011–2018 training period climatology. This shifts current observations back into the model’s training feature distribution. See site/scripts/apply_climate_delta.py for implementation.
